title: Quasi-affine morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-affine morphism of schemes [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism, def-pc-scheme], where a quasi-affine scheme means a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. For every morphism $g:S\prime\to S$, the projection $X\times_S S\prime\to S\prime$ from the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is quasi-affine in the same sense. No finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the forward implication of [lem-trf-quasi-affine-relative-spec-embedding] to $f$. Obtain a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebra $\mathcal A$, its relative spectrum $\pi:Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\to S$, and a quasi-compact open immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ with $\pi\circ i=f$.

source.place: Tag 01SO, first paragraph of proof, invoking Tag 01SM (lemma-characterize-quasi-affine)

proof.text: Put $Y'=Y\times_S S\prime$ and $X'=X\times_S S\prime$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $X'$ with $X\times_Y Y'$: a map from a scheme $T$ to either scheme is precisely a pair $(a:T\to X,b:T\to S\prime)$ satisfying $fa=gb$, since the map $T\to Y'$ is forced to be $(ia,b)$. These identifications preserve the maps to $Y'$ and $S\prime$. Thus the induced $i':X'\to Y'$ is the base change of $i$. It is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and is quasi-compact separately by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), because $i$ is quasi-compact. In particular these conclusions impose no condition on $g$.

source.place: Tag 01SO, second paragraph of proof; Schemes Tags 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion) and 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-spec-base-change] to $g$ and $\mathcal A$. It supplies the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{S\prime}$-algebra $g^*\mathcal A$ and an isomorphism $\Phi:\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S\prime}(g^*\mathcal A)\xrightarrow{\sim}Y'$ over $S\prime$. Compose $i'$ with $\Phi^{-1}$; identifying the target via this isomorphism gives a quasi-compact open immersion $X'\hookrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S\prime}(g^*\mathcal A)$ over $S\prime$. The open-subscheme image and the inverse images of affine opens are unchanged up to isomorphism, so openness and quasi-compactness are preserved by this identification.

source.place: Tag 01SO, base-changed relative-spectrum identification; Constructions Tag 01LX (lemma-spec-properties), base-change clause

proof.text: The converse implication of [lem-trf-quasi-affine-relative-spec-embedding], with base $S\prime$ and algebra $g^*\mathcal A$, now says that $X'\to S\prime$ is quasi-affine. The chosen map $X'\to S\prime$ is the fibre-product projection throughout Steps 2–3. No finite-presentation hypothesis has been used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01SO, lemma-base-change-quasi-affine, entire proof; Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine; Schemes Tags 01JY and 01K5; Constructions Tag 01LX
